title: Cold-leaching extraction for obtaining bacterial inhibitory substances
author: Catherine Cesa-Luna
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhs3j6gn

steps.title: Prepare solid LB medium
steps.instruction: Make Luria‑Bertani agar by adding per litre: 10 g peptone, 0.5 g yeast extract, and 10 g sodium chloride; autoclave and pour approximately 10 mL into each small agar plate.

steps.title: Place culture on nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: Lay a sterile 0.22 µm nitrocellulose filter membrane on the agar surface, pipette 100 µL of an overnight producer‑strain culture (~6.5 × 10⁷ CFU mL⁻¹) onto the membrane, and let the membrane surface dry.

steps.title: Incubate plates for growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates with the membrane‑covered agar for 30 h at 30 °C.

steps.title: Transfer agar to ethanol
steps.instruction: After incubation, remove the membranes, cut all agar from each plate with a sterile scalpel, and place the agar into a conical‑bottom centrifuge tube that already contains filtered absolute ethanol, using a ratio of 3 g agar per 1 mL ethanol.

steps.title: Cold extraction
steps.instruction: Seal the tubes and incubate them for 48 h at 4 °C to allow extraction of inhibitory substances into the ethanol.

steps.title: Separate supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 5000 rpm for 12 min at 4 °C, then transfer the clear supernatant to fresh tubes.

steps.title: Optional concentration
steps.instruction: If a more concentrated extract is needed, evaporate the ethanol using a rotary evaporator; afterwards test both the aqueous residue and the remaining solvent phase for activity to ensure no compounds were lost.

steps.title: Sterilize final extract
steps.instruction: Filter the collected extract through a 0.22 µm pore‑size filter to sterilize it.

steps.title: Assess antimicrobial activity
steps.instruction: Evaluate the sterile extract by a double‑layer agar assay or an agar‑well diffusion method; optionally calculate arbitrary units (AU mL⁻¹). Include control extracts obtained from agar that had no bacterial growth.
